subclass_note: Step 1.1 cited all ten facts [L1]-[L10] in one bracket while using two of them; step 4.1 made the inference "normal in the kernel and hence normal in G", which is invalid in general and is licensed here only by [L9] (cor-normal-sylow-subgroup-of-a-normal-subgroup-is-normal), which step 4.1 does not cite. The fact is declared and true of this situation, so the mathematics holds and the gap is inside the 30-second rule; but because step 1.1's shotgun bracket claimed every fact, the contract's input map recorded [L9] as used at a step that does not use it, and the coverage check passed without any step accounting for the actual inference. Recorded, not repaired: the step numbering and citation redistribution would move the item hash for a defect that is presentational, and step 8 is the wrong place to discover it.

prevention.ref: proof-contract could flag a single step whose input bracket names more than half the item's declared facts: a shotgun bracket satisfies the exactly-once input map while attributing every fact to one step.

subject: thm-jordan-holder-theorem-for-modules
subclass_note: Reader 2 rewrote this proof under R2-7 and the rewrite is correct — I re-derived the whole induction, including that the A != B branch's series of C has length n-2 and that the two factor multisets agree via A/C ~ M/B and B/C ~ M/A. But its closing sentence, "This also covers n=1, when C=0", is wrong about its own branch: at n=1 the module M is simple, so its only maximal proper submodule is 0 and A=B necessarily, making the A != B branch vacuous rather than covered. Taking the sentence at face value would put step 4.1's length count at n-2 = -1. The case is genuinely handled, by step 2.1's A = B branch.

prevention.ref: A reader that rewrites a proof owns its boundary sentences too; the rewrite was checked for validity but its inherited closing clause was not re-derived against the new argument.

subject: finite-smoke registers zero obligations across all 175 proof-bearing items in batches 1-3
subclass_note: finite-smoke.mjs reports "0 error(s), 0 check(s) over 0/26, 0/90, 0/59 item(s) carrying obligations" — it runs, exits zero and checks nothing, in three batches whose content is unusually rich in bounded finite claims: Sylow counts for groups of order at most fifteen, S_4, A_5 and Aff(Z/5); the length of Z/p^k; the reciprocity table for small odd primes; square-root counts modulo n; the order of Aut((Z/p)^2). These are exactly the claims a bounded countermodel search can falsify. The gate is green because nobody registered an obligation, which is indistinguishable in the output from a gate that searched and found nothing. CLOSED by Alpha contract-audit-3 (2026-08-17): the gate is live at 4 checks over 324 scoped items, and gate-liveness now reports "live finite-smoke 4 checks" instead of VACUOUS. Selected, each after reading the item and picking the registry check that probes ITS claim: binomial-congruence-solution-count on thm-unit-square-criterion-modulo-odd-prime-powers (exactly two solution classes; the search computes gcd(phi(p^k),2)=2 against actual counts), on lem-nonsingular-square-root-lift-modulo-odd-prime-powers (non-unique lifting would push the count above two at p^(k+1)), and on thm-unit-square-criterion-modulo-two-powers (reaches the modulus-2 and modulus-4 clauses only; 2^k for k>=3 has no primitive root and is outside the search by construction); cyclic-subgroup-lagrange on ex-length-of-z-modulo-p-to-the-k (the chain terms are the subgroups generated by p^i, whose orders the check computes). Three of this row's named candidates were declined on evidence rather than covered: the Sylow data table for orders at most fifteen (no registry check computes n_p = 1 mod p or n_p | m), the reciprocity table (no check computes Legendre symbols), and the order of Aut((Z/p)^2) (its step 4.1 states the argument "makes no matrix-group identification", so matrix-ring-laws-mod-n would test a route the proof deliberately avoids). Batch 3 and batches 4-7 carry no check: field theory, measure theory, topology and complex analysis match no registry entry, and the two poset checks are existence-of-failure witnesses for meets, whereas batch 7 asserts limit creation positively and its one failure item is a coequalizer in Set versus Grp. Detail and evidence: research/frontier-15-alpha-contract-audit.md.

prevention.ref: The tool-change half this row asked for already exists and is what caught the vacuity: gate-liveness.mjs distinguishes "searched, found nothing" from "no obligation registered" and reports VACUOUS with a nonzero exit, and the autopilot routes that vacuity to a contract-audit Alpha for check SELECTION (commit 1a63bc0b). What remained was the selection itself, which is judgement and is now done. finite-smoke.mjs also prints the coverage ratio (4/324) so the count can no longer be read as coverage.

subject: batches 1-2: 7 manifest rows disagreeing with the authored item frontmatter
subclass_note: Four batch-1 items declare a dependency the manifest lacks (prop-jacobi-symbol-on-units-is-a-homomorphism/thm-unit-criterion-modulo-n, thm-jacobi-map-kernel-and-square-subgroup/def-jacobi-symbol, cex-jacobi-symbol-one-does-not-imply-a-square/prop-unit-square-has-jacobi-symbol-one, ex-primes-dividing-x-squared-plus-three/thm-legendre-symbol-multiplicativity), left behind when reader 1 added the edges. In batch 2 the pair thm-lagrange + thm-number-of-bijections-of-a-finite-set sits on the manifest row for thm-groups-of-order-thirty-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup while the item that actually gained those inputs under R2-15 is thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup — a transcription slip that put the sync on the neighbouring theorem. Batch 3 had zero drift. All synced to the item frontmatter, which is the truth about what each proof cites.

prevention.ref: A manifest-vs-frontmatter diff belongs in the 6b gate set. Note for whoever writes it: compare YAML-parsed titles against JSON-parsed titles — comparing the raw frontmatter line against the parsed manifest value reports every backslash-bearing title as drift, which is how my first pass produced 30 false positives.

subject: 17 proof steps across the level name a check and perform none, and 4 contract boundary rows credit such a step as `checked`
subclass_note: The class is a numbered step whose entire content is an imperative naming work: "We treat the trivial $p$-subgroup and primes not dividing $|G|$." (thm-sylow-second-theorem 4.1), "We check the trivial quotient." (thm-fitting-subgroup-of-the-frattini-quotient 3.1), "We treat repeated terms and the zero module." (thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-artinian-modules 3.1), "Keep the two prime orderings and the order-twelve boundary case explicit." (thm-groups-of-order-p-squared-q-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup 4.1), "The preceding argument gives the conclusion under every hypothesis of the Statement." (4 items, contentless filler), "We check fields of characteristic two.", "We check the initial term $\mathbb Z$.", "We check the inverse map and the zero ring.", "Remove zero or repeated summands and include the zero-generated case.", "We apply orbit-stabiliser, including the unique/trivial Sylow case.", "The forward implication is published." (a repository status claim standing in for a step). Two items — prop-endomorphisms-form-a-ring and thm-endomorphism-ring-of-a-finite-direct-sum-as-hom-matrices — had NO proof at all: every numbered step was an announcement, one of them naming four ring axioms it never verified. Why this is a boundary defect and not only a prose defect: thm-sylow-second-theorem's contract marked `zero` and `degenerate` as `checked` with the evidence "is resolved in step 4.1", quoting the announcement verbatim. boundary-audit could not see it, because its `checked` detector only tests whether the credited step NUMBER exists in the proof, and 4.1 does exist. All 17 repaired: the real discharge written for each named case, and full proofs authored for the two items that had none. Each repaired item re-precheck'd, its contract entry regenerated, and proof-contract --strict re-run to 0 errors.

prevention.ref: Two tool changes, both live. (1) tools/announcement-steps.mjs, new: flags a numbered step whose every sentence opens by naming an activity and none of which states an outcome, splitting hits into `strong` and `weak` so a terse but real discharge is not swept up. Its verb list is grown from live misses, never guessed — the first version missed 2 of 3 known instances because inline math inside a NAMED case counted as work, and a later one missed "Keep the two prime orderings..." because `Keep` was absent. Cross-check it with an orthogonal scan (steps with no math, no relation symbol, under 170 chars) before trusting a zero result; that scan is noisy but it is what surfaced 3 further verbs. (2) tools/boundary-audit.mjs gains a fourth contradiction signal: a `checked` row crediting a step that IS an announcement, which is airtight because both halves are mechanical. Verified against a purpose-built fixture — it fires on the announcement-credited row and stays silent on the row crediting real work. NOT done, and deliberately: stripping the item's own title from the template-cluster key collapses frontier-15's interpolated rows into 31 clusters, but most are honest ('this item states no biconditional' is the true disposition for 45 items and has one natural phrasing), so it would make a precision-first gate noisy.

subject: thm-sylow-third-theorem chooses a Sylow subgroup with no dependency establishing that one exists, and declares a fact no step uses
subclass_note: Found by the independent DeepSeek refuter and confirmed from disk. Step 1.1 read "Let a Sylow subgroup $P$ act by conjugation on the Sylow set", which presupposes Syl_p(G) is nonempty — that is Sylow I, and thm-sylow-first-theorem appeared nowhere in `deps`. The item's own [L4] even says existence "is proved later". None of the five declared dependencies supplies it. Separately lem-product-with-normal-subgroup was declared as [L5] and used by no step. Both were invisible to proof-contract because step 1.1 carried a BLANKET citation of all five facts, which satisfies the every-fact-is-used check while telling the input map nothing true. Repaired: thm-sylow-first-theorem added to deps and to the facts block, step 1.1 rewritten to draw P from a set a cited fact has made nonempty, the unused fact removed, and steps 2.1 and 3.1 — which cited nothing at all while using Sylow II, the fixed-point congruence and the normalizer-index formula — written out with honest citations. The mathematics was correct throughout; only the dependency trace was false.

prevention.ref: The enabling pattern is the blanket citation: a first step listing every fact in the item, which makes `citation-uses` and `step-entry-input-omitted` vacuously satisfied for facts no step actually uses. Seen on at least 8 batch-2 items (thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-... cites 12 at step 1.1, cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five cites 15, ex-heisenberg-... cites 12). A proof-contract check worth writing: flag a step whose input list names more than N facts AND is the only step naming most of them; the honest cases are rare and can be upheld on the record like a boundary row.

subject: thm-sylow-second-theorem's title stated Sylow II with no finiteness marker
subclass_note: Reported as FATAL by the independent DeepSeek refuter, which supplied a correct counterexample: in the infinite dihedral group the maximal 2-subgroups <r^n s> split into two conjugacy classes by the parity of n, since conjugation sends r^n s to r^(n+2k) s or r^(2j-n) s. I verified that computation and it is right for the general notion of Sylow subgroup. I adjudicate it NONFATAL rather than fatal, on two pieces of evidence the refuter did not have: this library's def-sylow-p-subgroup is stated only for finite G, so the title's phrase cannot be read outside finite groups in-library; and a self-tested scan of the level found six other titles using the same convention (cor-sylow-subgroup-normal-iff-unique, thm-normalizer-of-a-sylow-normalizer, thm-frattini-argument, cor-frattini-subgroup-is-contained-in-the-fitting-subgroup, ex-a-four-is-not-nilpotent, cor-length-is-additive-in-short-exact-sequences). It was underspecified, not false in the library's own vocabulary. Title still amended to "in a finite group" as step-6 polish, because Sylow I and Sylow III both carry the marker and the title should stand alone in the index and flowchart, where the reader has not opened the definition.

prevention.ref: The scan that produced the six-item convention finding was itself broken on first run and returned zero hits — its `titleFinite` regex matched the very title it was meant to flag, so the empty result was meaningless. It only became evidence after a self-test asserting that the known-bad title flags and the repaired one clears. Any title/statement hypothesis-drift scan should carry that self-test inline; a zero-hit scan with no positive control is not a finding.

subject: risk-report reported 125 items unreviewed while 33 of them carried complete Alpha reviews under the wrong key
subclass_note: risk-report --require-reviewed demands risk_review.notes; Alpha-a had written its dispositions under risk_review.disposition. The 33 rows were substantive, per-item and in several cases recorded confirmed-fatal repairs with their own ledger rows — they were not missing work, they were a field-name mismatch, and the gate could not tell the two apart. I read all 33 before touching them and renamed the key; no rationale was written, weakened or invented to clear the gate. The remaining 92 were genuinely unreviewed and were read and reviewed individually. Recorded because the failure mode is worth naming: a gate that reports 'missing' cannot distinguish absent work from misfiled work, and the honest response to a large missing-count is to read the artifacts before assuming the work was never done.

prevention.ref: risk-report could distinguish the two cases cheaply: if contracts[id].risk_review exists but lacks `notes`, emit a distinct code (risk-review-malformed) naming the keys it did find, instead of the same risk-review-missing it emits for an absent block. The remedy line for the two is different — one is 'do the review', the other is 'rename the key' — and conflating them cost a full re-read of 33 completed reviews.

subject: 518 boundary rows across 88 batch-2 items are generated from the item's title and statement rather than written as dispositions
subclass_note: 26 items have a worksheet that is generated end to end and 62 are partly generated; batches 1 and 3-7 have none, so this is one Beta's habit and not a level-wide convention. The shape is "<title>: <stock clause for this axis> for \u201c<statement>\u201d", with `not_applicable` reasons drawn from a fixed set of seven phrasings ('has no set, family, sum, product, or series allowed to be empty', 'is a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional', ...) and `checked` evidence reading 'is resolved in step X.Y: "<verbatim step text>"'. boundary-audit's template detector reports NO cluster over these 518 rows, because interpolating each item's own title and statement makes every row textually unique — the normalizer strips the id and quoted spans but not the title. The independent DeepSeek refuter hit the same class from the other side on fs-finite-nilpotent-and-solvable-groups-coincide, whose iff-forward and iff-reverse rows call the claim 'a one-way assertion rather than a biconditional' when 'finite nilpotent and finite solvable groups are the same' is plainly an equivalence; I confirmed that from disk. NOT repaired at scale: rewriting 518 rows as real dispositions is the owning Beta's work with its sources to hand, and a bulk rewrite by me would reproduce the original defect in a new hand. The four rows that credited an announcement step ARE repaired, via f15-a-rr-001. STEP-9 SWEEP, STILL OPEN. Its recorded closing condition is a rewrite of the batch-2 boundary worksheets by the owning Beta, and no Beta runs at step 9, so the condition is not met and the row stays open deliberately. What step 9 DID establish, so the owner is not reading a bare 'unfinished': (a) the measurement in this row's prevention field was implemented — 454 of batch 2's 720 boundary rows match a stock tail or the 'is resolved in step X.Y:' frame under a conservative detector, 7 items fully generated and 81 partly; (b) boundary-audit still reports 0 template clusters and 0 contradicted over those 720 rows, confirming the interpolated title defeats its normalizer; (c) an independent targeted detector was run across ALL SEVEN batches for the one sub-class whose falsity is airtight — a not_applicable iff row on an item whose Statement carries two directions — returning 18 candidates, 16 over-fires and 2 real, both in batch 2, both now repaired (f15-S9-006); (d) NEITHER of the two concealed a mathematical defect: each item's own proof discharges exactly the obligation its row denied existed. So the residue is contract quality, not a hidden fatal defect, on the evidence available at step 9. What remains is the ~450 generated rows themselves, and rewriting them at scale is still the owning Beta's work with its sources to hand. OWNER ACCEPTANCE (2026-08-17, in-session): publish without the batch-2 worksheet rework — the mathematics and dependencies are cleared (86/86 fatals repaired, 398/398 current judge pairs, closure with no allowances); the targeted detector found 2 real false rows in 18 candidates and neither concealed a mathematical defect. The rework remains available to any future cycle via the recorded task file.

prevention.ref: The measurement is a 30-line script: count rows whose reason matches one of the seven stock tails or the 'is resolved in step X.Y:' frame, then group by item. Items at 8/8 are the ones to route back. Making boundary-audit itself fail on this needs care — stripping the title from the cluster key does collapse the rows, but it also collapses 45 honest 'this item states no biconditional' rows, and this tool's stated design is precision over recall because a detector firing on a third of the corpus trains readers to skim it.

subject: cor-classification-of-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five [L11] stops mid-clause at "and the resulting map.", so the biconditional it states has no right-hand conclusion and licenses nothing
subclass_note: The cited thm-internal-external-semidirect-product-equivalence states that N normal, G=NH, N cap H = 1 hold iff conjugation restricts to an action alpha and the resulting map Phi : N rtimes_alpha H -> G, (n,h) |-> nh IS AN ISOMORPHISM carrying the canonical factors onto N and H. The Facts line reproduced the antecedent and the first conjunct of the consequent and then ended with the words 'and the resulting map.' — no predicate. Step 3.1 concludes 'the internal product is G iso C_5 x H' and cites [L11] for it, so the step's stated support asserts nothing about the map at all. The mathematics of the item is correct: with N_5 normal, G = N_5 H, N_5 cap H = 1 and the conjugation action trivial (step 2.1, since gcd(21,4)=1), L11+L12 do give G iso C_5 x H. What was wrong is the citation, and only the citation. Not caught by citation-fidelity.mjs: the contract's recorded quote for L11 is the cited item's full statement section (itself cut at the tool's 400-char cap) and it does appear in the cited item, so --fail-on-missing-quote passes. Not caught by truncated-citation.mjs either: that detector compares a fact line against the cited section as a PREFIX and flags short prefixes, and this line is not a prefix — it paraphrases the antecedent before truncating, so the ratio heuristic never fires. The gap is that no gate compares the ITEM's fact line against the CONTRACT's recorded quote; both are checked against the cited item and neither against each other.

prevention.ref: A detector comparing each item's [F#]/[L#] line against its own contract row's `quote` would catch this class directly, and it is the one comparison the existing pair of tools does not make: citation-fidelity checks quote-vs-cited-item, truncated-citation checks factline-vs-cited-item, neither checks factline-vs-quote. A cheap first cut: flag any fact line ending in a determiner or bare noun phrase ('the resulting map.', 'the following holds.') before its citation parenthesis.

subject: thm-groups-of-order-one-hundred-five-have-a-normal-sylow-subgroup [L4] appends "le H" to the kernel equation, which thm-left-coset-action-and-its-kernel does not state
subclass_note: The published statement is ker rho = Core_G(H), full stop. The fact line printed ker rho = Core_G(H) le H, and step 3.1 uses exactly that extra clause twice — 'has kernel K subseteq H' and 'K le H gives 3 = [G:H] | [G:K]'. So the inflation is load-bearing, not decorative. It is nonfatal rather than fatal because Core_G(H) le H is immediate from def-core-of-a-subgroup (the intersection of all conjugates includes the g=1 term) and is stated outright by the published lem-core-is-largest-normal-subgroup-contained, which sits on group-actions-and-cayleys-theorem — a page this one already requires. Repaired by restoring [L4] to the source statement and adding [L13] citing lem-core-is-largest-normal-subgroup-contained for K le H, with that id added to deps and step 3.1's input list. The contract entry was regenerated, and its L4 quote had been correct all along, which is the second time in this run that the contract was faithful and the item was not.

prevention.ref: Same missing comparison as f15-6c-001: fact line versus its own contract quote. Here the contract quote is verbatim-correct and the item's line has one extra relational atom appended inside the same display, so a diff of the two would have printed it as a one-token addition.

published source, Statement — prints no inclusion

subject: thm-one-step-simultaneous-root-extension [L4] reads "is finite, and therefore algebraic" while thm-finitely-generated-algebraic-extensions-are-finite states only finiteness
subclass_note: The 'therefore algebraic' half is what step 4.1 actually needs — the whole point of that step is to conclude L/F is algebraic — so the inflation is load-bearing. The bridging fact, every finite field extension is algebraic, is published as thm-finite-field-extensions-are-algebraic on algebraic-extensions-degree-and-finite-fields, which this page's requires closure already reaches and which a sibling item on the same page (cor-finite-extension-of-a-perfect-field-is-simple) already cites correctly. Repaired by restoring [L4] to the source statement verbatim, adding [L6] for the bridging theorem, adding it to deps, and splitting step 4.1's reasoning across the two facts.

prevention.ref: A fact line joining two claims with 'and therefore' or 'hence' while naming a single source is a mechanically detectable shape; when the trailing claim is not a substring-equivalent of anything in the cited statement, it needs its own citation. This is the same factline-versus-quote diff as f15-6c-001 and f15-6c-002.

subject: thm-monads-on-a-preorder-are-exactly-closure-operators [L1] attributes the natural-transformation criterion Fp le Gp to prop-preorders-as-categories-and-monotone-maps-as-functors, which states only that functors between preorders are monotone maps
subclass_note: The added clause is the entire mechanism of the theorem: steps 1.1 and 1.2 read eta as the family p le Tp and mu as T(Tp) le Tp, and both cite [L1] for the right to do so. The cited proposition does say 'a preorder determines a category with at most one morphism between any two objects', and the criterion follows from that in two lines — a morphism Fp -> Gp exists exactly when Fp le Gp, and naturality squares commute for want of a second arrow — so it is nonfatal. Repaired by restoring [L1] to the source statement, which includes the at-most-one-morphism clause, and deriving the natural-transformation criterion inline in step 1.1, where the derivation is now visible instead of hidden in a citation. Step 1.2 already used the at-most-one-arrow clause explicitly for the monad diagrams, so the item was half-honest about its route already.

prevention.ref: citation-faithfulness-screen.mjs did flag this line as a candidate (L1 -> prop-preorders-as-categories-and-monotone-maps-as-functors: Rightarrow, leq — two operators the cited statement never mentions), and it was among the 42 candidates the run's earlier stages left unread. The detector worked; the routing did not. The cheap change is to require a written disposition per candidate at 6b, the way risk-report requires a risk_review, rather than printing candidates for an optional read.

subject: ex-the-ultrafilter-monad-on-a-finite-set [L3] restates thm-ultrafilter-lemma without its "Assume the Axiom of Choice" hypothesis
subclass_note: The published thm-ultrafilter-lemma opens 'Assume the Axiom of Choice' and its own remarks account for exactly where that is spent (Zorn at step 4.1). The fact line printed 'Every proper filter is contained in an ultrafilter' flat, then wrote 'assuming this principle' for the second half — so the choice cost was attached to the consequence rather than to the theorem that incurs it, and a reader could take clause 1 for a ZF theorem. Nonfatal because step 4.1 does say 'Assuming [L3]', so nothing downstream claims a choice-free result. Repaired by printing the hypothesis on the theorem where the source prints it, and by matching the source's 'every filter' rather than 'every proper filter' (def-filter in this library already excludes the empty set, so the two agree, but the source's wording is the one to reproduce). This matters more than usual on this page because the batch-4 and batch-7 items around it keep explicit choice ledgers.

prevention.ref: A cited item whose statement section opens with a bolded 'Assume the Axiom of Choice' / 'Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice' and whose citing fact line contains no choice word is a two-line grep, and the corpus already marks those hypotheses in a fixed bolded form. Batch 4 gets this right in five places (thm-countable-union-of-countable, thm-countable-subsets-of-omega-one-are-bounded, thm-well-ordering-theorem, thm-cardinal-power-set-and-cantor, thm-zorn), which is what makes the one miss detectable as a miss rather than a convention.

subject: cex-connected-domain-need-not-be-star-shaped [L1] cites lem-punctured-rn-is-polygonally-connected for an arbitrary puncture R^n minus {p}, while the published lemma states only R^n minus {0}
subclass_note: Generalising the puncture from the origin to an arbitrary point is true but needs translation-invariance of polygonal connectedness, which the cited lemma does not supply and no other declared dependency states. It is not load-bearing here: the counterexample is U = C minus {0}, so the p = 0 instance is the only one used, and step 1.1 invokes [L1] on exactly that set. Repaired by restating [L1] as the source states it. Recorded rather than waved through because the same inflated line copied onto a page that punctures somewhere other than the origin would be a real gap, and the item text is what gets copied.

prevention.ref: Same factline-versus-quote diff as f15-6c-001 through 003; here the difference is a single substituted symbol inside a set-builder, which a token-level diff of the two strings surfaces immediately.

subject: cor-algebraic-closures-are-isomorphic-over-the-base
subclass_note: The title read 'Assuming Choice, any two algebraic closures are base-isomorphic, generally nonuniquely' and the Statement repeated the claim as 'Such an isomorphism generally need not be unique.' Step 3.1 of the same item says the opposite about its own scope: 'The argument proves existence only and makes no uniqueness assertion.' Nonuniqueness is therefore asserted in the reader-facing title and Statement of a landmark item and established nowhere in it. Repaired by narrowing (owner repair 3): the title now stops at 'base-isomorphic' and the Statement says 'No uniqueness of the isomorphism is asserted.' The claim is not lost to the library -- fs-algebraic-closure-is-unique-up-to-unique-isomorphism, on the same pair, actually proves nonuniqueness by exhibiting the nonidentity Q-automorphism of an algebraic closure of Q carrying a root of x^2+1 to its negative, and its own [L4] already restates this corollary as existence only. The narrowed Statement and that consumer's citation now agree exactly.

prevention.ref: the phrase was in the step-1 scaffold title verbatim; a title asserting a second claim ('generally nonuniquely', 'and not conversely', 'necessarily') is checkable at step 3 against the strategy, before any proof exists

subject: thm-separable-closures-exist-and-are-isomorphic-over-the-base
subclass_note: The Statement read 'Any two separable closures are F-isomorphic, generally nonuniquely', while step 2.2 ends 'The construction does not assert uniqueness.' The proof builds one F-embedding and shows it is onto; it neither proves nor exhibits nonuniqueness. Unlike the algebraic-closure case the scaffold title was clean, so the clause was added at authoring. Repaired by narrowing: the Statement now ends 'Any two separable closures are F-isomorphic. No uniqueness of the isomorphism is asserted.'

prevention.ref: same shape as frontier-15-S8-01 on the same page; when one item in a pair acquires an unproved 'generally nonuniquely' the sibling should be checked in the same pass

subject: thm-extension-generated-by-separable-elements-is-separable
subclass_note: Step 1.2 built the tower F <= F(s_1) <= ... <= F(s_1,...,s_r), showed only that each s_j has separable minimal polynomial over the preceding field, and then applied [L1] (thm-separability-is-transitive) to conclude the whole subextension is separable over F. Transitivity requires each adjacent extension to be separable elementwise; 'the generator is separable' gives that only via the one-generator case of the very theorem being proved, so the inference was circular. Both lanes found it independently and stated it precisely. (2) 'Substituting the group-word identities into the same multiplication law turns them into associativity, the unit laws and the inverse laws' compresses four instantiations of a T(a) = a mu_A, one of which is materially different: for W = [[x],[x^{-1}]] the two entries are both POSITIVE letters of the alphabet TA, so W is reduced and T(a)(W) is the honest two-letter word, while mu_A multiplies them inside F(A) where they cancel to the empty word. That asymmetry is where the identity comes from and the text does not flag it. Used correctly, not assumed. NOT repaired: step 8 is fatal-only under R1, and this is exposition rather than a gap.

The old step 1.3 asserted the restriction-of-scalars determinant identity. The repair proves transitivity from restriction fibres, embedding formulas, and multiplicativity of separable and inseparable degrees.

The old maximal-subgroup argument falsely made G/H simple. The repair separates each nonidentity automorphism by a character obtained from the invariant-factor decomposition, then applies cyclic Kummer theory to its fixed field.

subclass_note: tools/reflow.mts documents that 'each numbered step must sit on one physical line' and joins a step's soft-wrapped continuation lines into one line. precheck.mts credits a step only when its line ENDS with a bracketed justification tag from PROP_TAG. [L2, L3, step 1.1]') and the step continues on following lines, so whole-batch precheck passed (15201 items, 0 failing on the pre-5a tree). Running the canonical reflow tool on five such items merged each step into one line whose trailing bracket was a content tag ('[finite counting]', '[finite-dimensional duality, square-sum Holder]') or no tag at all, producing bad-tag/untagged-steps failures on items that had passed. Local remedy used here: re-split each step line immediately after its first bracketed tag, restoring the passing convention for the five edited items. The tool and the checker disagree about the canonical step shape; one of them needs the owner's decision (fix reflow to split after the first tag, or extend PROP_TAG to the corpus's content tags). RESOLVED at 5b-cross (phase-2-next-18, 2026-09-14): tools/reflow.mts now keeps a numbered step's line when it already ends with a bracketed group, instead of joining its continuation into it, so the tag the line-based checker reads stays at the end of the step's physical line. The alternative remedy (extending PROP_TAG in the app repo) remains open and does not conflict with this fix.

subject: def-logarithmic-potential-and-energy
finding: The remark says energy is defined when “at least one” of the positive and negative kernel integrals is finite, with value in (-infinity,+infinity]. Let rho_n be normalized arclength on the circle of radius 1/4 centered at e^n, and let sigma be the probability mixture with weights proportional to 1/n^2. Distinct circles are more than distance 1 apart, so the positive-part integral is only the same-circle contribution and is finite (each same-circle integral is log 4, weighted by a summable multiple of 1/n^4). For n<m, cross-circle distances are at least e^m/2, so the negative-part integral is bounded below by a positive multiple of sum_m (m-log 2)/m^2 times sum_{n<m}1/n^2, which diverges. Thus one part is finite, as the stated criterion allows, but the energy is -infinity, outside the claimed range.
